The note states explicitly: b (S0224) is 'closely related to but more specific/operational than the general pramana-four-knowledge-sources mapping' -- b specializes/operationalizes a's general four-pramana epistemology into a concrete knowledge-producing-process registry.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: Wrong if b's registry-of-processes proposal is shown to be motivated independently of the four-pramana (Pratyaksa/Anumana/Upamana/Sabda) framework.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: PARTIALLY-COMPATIBLE reflects that six-pramana is a taxonomically well-known superset of four-pramana within the Nyaya tradition itself (domain-level compatibility), independent of whether these two specific corpus research threads are actually connected -- which remains genuinely unresolved per the batch's own uncertainty note.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: group_evidence (G0098) explicitly frames this as unresolved: B's six-pramana model (adding Arthapatti/postulation and Anupalabdhi/absence to the classical four) 'may be the same recurring pramana research thread as pramana-four-knowledge-sources... under a different (six-source) taxonomy, or a distinct model -- unresolved.' Zero dual-labeled rows. Content confirms two separate research threads: A's rows (S0219/S0220/S0222/S0224/S0225/S0460/S1312) build a KnowledgeOS-specific four-pramana mapping and INV-KOS-Pramana-001 from Tarka-Sangraha/Nyaya extraction files; B's rows (S0499-S0525) belong to a separate ten-lens synthesis series (Ganesha/Pramana/Leonardo/Krishna/Zero) that treats Pramana as one of ten lenses, without citing or extending A's specific INV-KOS-Pramana-001 work.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row in B's ten-lens series explicitly citing or extending A's INV-KOS-Pramana-001 (rather than independently re-deriving pramana content from the same underlying Nyaya tradition) would establish real continuity.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both label's rows come from the SAME source document (S0219): A's rows introduce the general four-pramana model (Pratyaksa/Anumana/Upamana/Sabda); B's rows, later in the same document, elaborate specifically on distinguishing Tarka from Anumana, including candidate invariant TARKA-003: 'reasoning that tests claims (tarka) is distinct from reasoning that produces knowledge (anumana)' -- a direct refinement of the boundary of A's Anumana category.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If TARKA-003 is a self-contained finding about Tarka alone with no bearing on how Anumana itself is defined, this overstates the connection; the shared source and explicit tarka-vs-anumana boundary language argue for the stronger reading.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Pratyaksa Perception ... Anumana Inference ... Upamana Comparison ... Sabda Testimony ... KnowledgeOS Parallel: Observation, Reasoning from evidence, Pattern matching/analogical reasoning, Authority/expert testimony
rationale_evidence.statement: Presents the four Nyaya pramanas with a proposed KnowledgeOS parallel mapping and notes perception is treated as fundamental because the other three depend on prior cognition; concludes KnowledgeOS's existing Evidence/Authority/Reasoning distinctions could be given a structured epistemological framework via this mapping.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Unlike Western formal logic (divorced from epistemology), Nyaya integrates logic with explicit knowledge sources.
rationale_evidence.statement: Comparative table contrasting Tarka Shastra/Nyaya against Western epistemic logic across knowledge sources, reasoning structure, contradiction handling, authority, doubt, and goal, concluding Nyaya offers a more integrated epistemology+logic+authority framework than Western formal logic alone.

rationale_evidence.anchor: `EvidenceLinks` (l. 209) carries *"evidence references + **acquisition method** + reliability conditions."* **Acquisition method is already there.**
rationale_evidence.statement: Session 1 claims three separate carriers an evidence/claim reference may need: route (S1-F035, by what epistemic means was this obtained, e.g. pratyaksa vs upamana), acquisition procedure (S1-F030), and role (S1-F029). This review disputes the count: EvidenceLinks (l.209) already carries evidence references plus acquisition method plus reliability conditions -- acquisition method is already in law -- and route is very close to acquisition method, so whether they are one carrier or two is the same semantic-denotation question left open at two prior reviews (S2-R-F029, S2-R-F030). The defensible composite is smaller: one carrier already in law (acquisition/route, possibly one thing) plus one genuinely absent carrier (role).
